record.paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
record.original_question: In online graph coloring, an algorithm receives the vertices of a graph one at a time and irrevocably assigns each new vertex a color using only the revealed subgraph and previous colors. For a graph G, chi_OL(G) is the smallest worst-case number of colors achievable by any online coloring algorithm. Is the class of all graphs online chi_OL-bounded, meaning that there exists an online coloring algorithm whose color use on every graph G is bounded by some function of chi_OL(G)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In online graph coloring, an algorithm is given the vertices of a finite simple graph $G$ one at a time in an order chosen by an adversary. When a vertex $v$ is revealed, the algorithm also learns all edges between $v$ and previously revealed vertices, and must irrevocably assign $v$ a positive integer color so that the resulting partial coloring is proper (adjacent vertices receive distinct colors). For a graph $G$, define $\chi_{OL}(G)$ to be the minimum, over all deterministic online coloring algorithms $A$, of the maximum, over all vertex presentation orders of $G$, of the number of colors used by $A$ on $G$.

A class $\mathcal{G}$ of graphs is said to be online $\chi_{OL}$-bounded if there exists a single online coloring algorithm $A$ (working on all graphs) and a function $f:\mathbb{N}	o\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $G\in\mathcal{G}$ and every presentation order of $V(G)$, the number of colors used by $A$ is at most $f(\chi_{OL}(G))$.

Question: Is the class of all finite simple graphs online $\chi_{OL}$-bounded?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears still open. Survey and research sources note that the existence of an online-competitive algorithm for all graphs (and even just for all bipartite graphs) is a long-standing open question stemming from work of Gyárfás and Lehel; competitive algorithms are known only for restricted classes (forests, certain $P_t$-free bipartite graphs, graphs of girth at least 5, etc.).

status_evidence.title: An On-line Competitive Algorithm for Coloring P8-free Bipartite Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: The existence of an on-line competitive algorithm for coloring bipartite graphs is a tantalizing open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Even for bipartite graphs, existence of an online-competitive algorithm is open, implying the general problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: On-Line and First Fit Colorings of Graphs — Gyárfás, Lehel
status_evidence.snippet: First-Fit is competitive (with an exponential bounding function) for graphs of girth at least 5.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial positive results for restricted classes are known.

status_evidence.title: Tight Bounds for Online Coloring of Basic Graph Classes (ESA 2017)
status_evidence.snippet: Tight bounds for online coloring of basic graph classes.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research focuses on online coloring of specific classes, with the general boundedness question unresolved.
